parts.text:
10 A ship of mass 8.4 × 107
kg is approaching a harbour with speed 16.4 m s–1. By using reverse
thrust it can maintain a constant total stopping force of 920 000 N.
How long will it take to stop?
A
15 seconds
B
150 seconds
C
25 minutes
D
250 minutes

hints: Notice the ship has initial momentum from $8.4 \times 10^7 \text{ kg}$ and $16.4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, and a constant opposing force of $920000 \text{ N}$ acts until velocity is zero.
Connect force and time through change in momentum: $F\Delta t = m\Delta v$, so stopping time is $t = mv/F$.
Calculate $t$ in seconds first, then divide by 60 to compare with the options given in seconds and minutes.
walkthrough: List the useful values: $m = 8.4 \times 10^7 \text{ kg}$, initial speed $u = 16.4 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, final speed $v = 0$, and stopping force $F = 920000 \text{ N}$.
Use impulse equals change in momentum for stopping: $F t = m(u - 0) = mu$, so $t = mu/F$.
Substitute with units: $t = (8.4 \times 10^7 \text{ kg})(16.4 \text{ m s}^{-1})/(9.2 \times 10^5 \text{ N})$.
Calculate numerator: $8.4 \times 10^7 \times 16.4 \approx 1.378 \times 10^9 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, then $t \approx 1.378 \times 10^9 / 9.2 \times 10^5 \approx 1500 \text{ s}$.
Convert seconds to minutes: $1500/60 \approx 25$ minutes, with constant deceleration of only about $0.011 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ because the mass is so large. This is option C.

A.explanation: 15 seconds is far too short and ignores the huge mass of $8.4 \times 10^7 \text{ kg}$ compared with the $920000 \text{ N}$ force.

B.explanation: 150 seconds is a factor of 10 too small, from an error with powers of 10 when dividing momentum by $920000 \text{ N}$.

C.explanation: A time of about $1500 \text{ s}$ equals 25 minutes, which matches $t = mv/F$ for the given mass, speed and stopping force.

D.explanation: 250 minutes is a factor of 10 too large, from confusing seconds with minutes or misplacing a power of 10.
